title: GoI Act 1935, 1937 Elections & Transfer of Power

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the First Round Table Conference:
1. It was convened after the report of the Simon Commission had been published.
2. The Indian National Congress did not participate in it.
3. B.R. Ambedkar did not attend it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Simon report came out in 1930 and the conference met in London from November 1930; Congress, engaged in Civil Disobedience, stayed away. Ambedkar did attend as a representative of the Depressed Classes, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q: Mahatma Gandhi attended the Second Round Table Conference in London in 1931 as the sole representative of the Congress. His participation was made possible by which of the following?
questions.e: After the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 1931) Civil Disobedience was suspended and the Congress agreed to attend the conference; the talks collapsed mainly over the communal question.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Poona Pact, 1932:
1. It replaced separate electorates for the Depressed Classes with reserved seats within the general electorate.
2. It increased the seats reserved for the Depressed Classes in the provincial legislatures from 71 to 147.
3. It was signed by Mahatma Gandhi himself in Yerwada jail.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Gandhi's fast against the Communal Award ended with the pact between Ambedkar and Hindu leaders; reserved seats rose from 71 to 147. Gandhi did not sign it; it was signed by leaders such as Madan Mohan Malaviya and Rajendra Prasad on behalf of caste Hindus.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q: The Joint Select Committee whose report formed the basis of the Government of India Act, 1935 was chaired by
questions.e: The committee (1933-34) examined the White Paper and was chaired by Lord Linlithgow, later Viceroy. Samuel Hoare, Secretary of State for India, piloted the Bill through Parliament, a common confusion.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Consider the following provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. Dyarchy was abolished in the provinces and introduced at the Centre.
2. The provisions relating to the All-India Federation came into force along with provincial autonomy in 1937.
3. Burma was separated from British India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Provinces got autonomy while certain Central subjects were reserved to the Governor-General. The federal part needed accession by princely states and never started, so statement 2 is wrong. Burma was separated in 1937.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 1

questions.q:
With reference to the Government of India Act, 1935, consider the following statements:
1. It provided for the establishment of a Federal Court.
2. It provided for Public Service Commissions at the Federal and provincial levels.
3. It provided for bicameral legislatures in all the provinces.
4. It vested residuary powers in the provincial legislatures.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Federal Court (1937) and the PSCs were created by the Act. Only six provinces got bicameral legislatures, and residuary powers lay with the Governor-General, not the provinces.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 1

questions.q: The Government of India Act, 1935 divided legislative subjects into three lists. The number of items in the Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists respectively was
questions.e: The Federal List had 59 items, the Provincial List 54 and the Concurrent List 36. This three-fold scheme was the model for the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 1
questions.h: Federal 59, Provincial 54, Concurrent 36: falling order after the Centre, with 36 'shared'.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The federal part of the Government of India Act, 1935 never came into operation.
Statement-II: The Act required a specified proportion of the princely states, by population and by seats in the Council of State, to accede before the federation could be inaugurated.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The federation depended on enough rulers acceding; because the princes did not reach the required threshold, the Centre continued to function under the earlier arrangement while only the provincial part began in 1937.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, approximately what share of the total population of British India was enfranchised?
questions.e: The franchise was widened on property, tax and educational qualifications, giving the vote to nearly one-tenth of the population. Universal adult franchise came only in 1950.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 1

questions.q: Who was the first Chief Justice of the Federal Court of India established in 1937 under the Government of India Act, 1935?
questions.e: Sir Maurice Gwyer headed the Federal Court at Delhi from 1937. Patrick Spens became Chief Justice later, in 1943, so he is a tempting distractor.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 1

questions.q: Jinnah's Fourteen Points (1929) were a direct response to which one of the following?
questions.e: The Nehru Report rejected separate electorates and weightage; Jinnah's amendments were turned down at the Calcutta All Parties Convention, after which he put forward the Fourteen Points. The Communal Award and the 1935 Act came later.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Communal Award
2. Poona Pact
3. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
4. Third Round Table Conference
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 1931), Communal Award (August 1932), Poona Pact (September 1932), and the Third Round Table Conference (November-December 1932, which Congress did not attend).
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence
questions.h: Pact, Award, Pact, Table: Irwin, Communal, Poona, Third RTC.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Lord Irwin's declaration of October 1929:
1. It stated that Dominion Status was the natural issue of India's constitutional progress.
2. It was made after the Simon Commission Report had been published.
3. It was made before the Lahore session of the Congress which adopted Purna Swaraj.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The declaration came in October 1929 and promised a Round Table Conference; Lahore (December 1929) followed. The Simon report was published only in 1930, so statement 2 is wrong.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: A. Communal Award; B. Gandhi-Irwin Pact; C. Poona Pact; D. August Offer
List-II: 1. Linlithgow; 2. Ramsay MacDonald; 3. Irwin; 4. B.R. Ambedkar
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: MacDonald announced the Award (1932), Irwin signed the 1931 Pact with Gandhi, Ambedkar negotiated the Poona Pact, and Linlithgow announced the August Offer in 1940.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: Abolition of the Council of India
Division of subjects into Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists
questions.e: Dyarchy, not responsible government, operated at the Centre, with defence and external affairs reserved to the Governor-General. The Council of India was abolished, provincial autonomy was introduced and the three-fold list system was created.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 1

questions.q: In the provincial elections held in 1937 under the Government of India Act, 1935, the Indian National Congress
o: won an absolute majority in five of the eleven provinces
won an absolute majority in all eleven provinces
won an absolute majority in Bengal and Punjab but failed in Madras
won a majority only in the Hindu-majority provinces of Bombay and Madras
questions.e: The Congress won clear majorities in five provinces (including Madras, Bihar, Orissa, United Provinces and Central Provinces) and was the largest party in some others. It was not in majority in Punjab or Bengal, where regional parties did well.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q: The 1936 session of the Indian National Congress, held in a village and presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, was at
questions.e: Faizpur (December 1936) was the first Congress session held in a village, and it adopted an agrarian programme ahead of the 1937 elections. Haripura (1938), Tripuri (1939) and Ramgarh (1940) came later.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India
questions.h: Faizpur: first village session, farmers first.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the provincial governments formed after the 1937 elections:
1. The Unionist Party formed the government in Punjab under Sikandar Hayat Khan.
2. In the United Provinces the Congress and the Muslim League formed a coalition ministry.
3. In Bengal, Fazlul Huq's Krishak Praja Party formed the ministry with the support of the Muslim League.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The League did not do well in Punjab or Bengal and had to work with regional parties. In the United Provinces the Congress declined a coalition with the League, a decision that Jinnah later used to charge the Congress with Hindu domination.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Statement-I: After the 1937 elections the Congress did not form a coalition ministry with the Muslim League in the United Provinces.
Statement-II: The Congress insisted that the League's legislators would be taken in only if they merged their party with the Congress and accepted its discipline.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Having won a clear majority in most provinces, the Congress was unwilling to share power on the League's terms and demanded that its members join the Congress, which the League refused. The episode widened the Congress-League gulf.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Congress ministries of 1937-39:
1. They released political prisoners and eased restrictions on civil liberties.
2. They enacted tenancy and debt relief legislation in several provinces.
3. They abolished the zamindari system in all the provinces they governed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The ministries had limited powers and finances, so they focused on civil liberties and agrarian relief such as tenancy amendments and debt conciliation. Zamindari abolition was not achieved in this period; it came after independence.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q: The 'Pirpur Report' of 1938, which charged the Congress ministries with oppression of Muslims, was published by
questions.e: The Pirpur Report (named after the Raja of Pirpur) was one of the League's reports, alongside the Shareef Report, alleging injustice to Muslims under Congress rule. Jinnah used them to build support before the Lahore Resolution.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q: The Wardha Scheme of Basic Education, taken up by the Congress ministries, was worked out in detail by a committee headed by
questions.e: After the Wardha Education Conference (1937) Gandhi's idea of education through a craft was elaborated by the Zakir Husain Committee. Muslim opposition to the Vidya Mandir scheme in some provinces fed communal tension.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q:
Match the Congress Premier with the province he headed after the 1937 elections:
List-I: A. C. Rajagopalachari; B. B.G. Kher; C. Dr. Khan Sahib; D. Govind Ballabh Pant
List-II: 1. Bombay; 2. Madras; 3. North-West Frontier Province; 4. United Provinces
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Rajagopalachari led Madras, B.G. Kher Bombay, Dr. Khan Sahib the NWFP and Pant the United Provinces. Under the 1935 Act the heads of provincial governments were styled Premiers.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q: After Subhas Chandra Bose resigned as Congress President in 1939 following his re-election at Tripuri, who was chosen to succeed him?
questions.e: Bose defeated Gandhi's candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Tripuri but could not work with the Working Committee, resigned, and later formed the Forward Bloc. Rajendra Prasad took over; Azad became President at Ramgarh in 1940.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
With reference to the end of the Congress ministries in 1939, consider the following statements:
1. The ministries resigned in protest against India being declared a belligerent in the Second World War without consultation.
2. Muhammad Ali Jinnah called upon Muslims to observe a 'Day of Deliverance' on the resignation.
3. The Muslim League joined the Congress in the protest and resigned its own ministries.
4. The Governors then took over the administration of the provinces under Section 93 of the 1935 Act.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Linlithgow's declaration of war without consulting Indian leaders led to the resignations in October-November 1939, and Jinnah observed the Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939. The League did not join the protest; Jinnah in fact celebrated the resignations. Governors then took over under Section 93.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Lahore Resolution of the Muslim League, March 1940:
1. It was moved by A.K. Fazlul Huq.
2. It explicitly used the term 'Pakistan' for the proposed Muslim state.
3. It demanded that the Muslim-majority zones in the north-west and east be grouped to constitute independent states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Fazlul Huq, then Bengal's Premier, moved the resolution. It spoke of 'independent states' in the north-western and eastern zones; the word 'Pakistan' was not in the text and was attached to it by the press and its opponents.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
With reference to the August Offer of 1940, consider the following statements:
1. It was announced by Viceroy Linlithgow.
2. It promised an immediate constituent assembly of Indians to frame the Constitution.
3. It assured the minorities that power would not be transferred to a government whose authority was denied by large and powerful elements in national life.
4. It proposed expansion of the Viceroy's Executive Council with more Indians.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The offer promised Dominion Status in the future, a War Advisory Council and an expanded Executive Council, and a constitution-making body only after the war. The assurance to minorities in effect gave the League a veto, which is why the Congress rejected the offer while Jinnah welcomed this part.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q: In the Individual Satyagraha launched by Gandhi in October 1940, who was chosen as the first satyagrahi?
questions.e: Individual Satyagraha was a symbolic protest against the war, with selected persons shouting anti-war slogans. Vinoba Bhave was first, followed by Jawaharlal Nehru as the second and Brahma Datt as the third.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Cripps Mission, 1942:
1. Sir Stafford Cripps came as a member of Churchill's War Cabinet.
2. It offered Dominion Status after the war with the right to secede from the Commonwealth.
3. It offered a provision allowing a province not willing to join the Indian Union to remain out and frame a separate constitution.
4. It offered immediate Indian control over defence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The draft promised Dominion Status after the war, a Constituent Assembly elected by provincial assemblies and the option of non-accession for provinces, but defence stayed with the British during the war. The non-accession clause was read as a seed of Pakistan.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Congress rejected the Cripps proposals of 1942.
Statement-II: The proposals offered only post-war Dominion Status, left defence in British hands and allowed provinces to stay out of the Union.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Congress wanted a National Government with real powers, including defence, immediately; the Cripps draft gave neither. The provincial non-accession clause also violated its demand for unity.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Quit India Movement:
1. The resolution was passed by the AICC at Bombay on 8 August 1942.
2. Gandhi gave the slogan 'Do or Die' at that session.
3. The Communist Party of India actively supported the movement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The resolution was passed at Gowalia Tank and top leaders were arrested the next morning. The CPI, following the 'People's War' line after the USSR was attacked, opposed the movement and lost ground among nationalists.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
The parallel governments set up during the Quit India Movement included
1. Ballia in eastern United Provinces
2. Tamluk in Bengal
3. Satara in Maharashtra
Which of the above are correct?
questions.e: Ballia (Chittu Pandey), Tamluk (Jatiya Sarkar) and Satara (Prati Sarkar, led by leaders such as Nana Patil) all saw short-lived or lasting parallel administrations in 1942-44.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India
questions.h: Ballia, Tamluk, Satara: B-T-S, three parallel states.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the C. Rajagopalachari (CR) Formula of 1944:
1. It proposed a plebiscite after the war in contiguous Muslim-majority areas of the north-west and east to decide on separation.
2. It proposed that only Muslims in those areas would vote in the plebiscite.
3. Jinnah rejected it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The formula envisaged a plebiscite of all inhabitants in the areas concerned, with the League cooperating in an interim government. Jinnah rejected it, wanting only Muslims to vote and Pakistan to be conceded before independence.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Simla Conference of 1945 failed to produce a new Executive Council.
Statement-II: Jinnah insisted that all Muslim members of the Council must be nominated by the Muslim League alone.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Wavell's plan proposed parity between caste Hindus and Muslims; the Congress could not accept being treated only as a Hindu party and Jinnah would not accept non-League Muslims. The deadlock ended the conference in July 1945.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q: The three INA officers tried first at the Red Fort in November 1945 were
o: Mohan Singh, Shah Nawaz Khan and G.S. Dhillon
Shah Nawaz Khan, P.K. Sahgal and G.S. Dhillon
Dr A.C. Chatterji, Mohan Singh and P.K. Sahgal
Rash Behari Bose, P.K. Sahgal and Shah Nawaz Khan
questions.e: The first trial put a Muslim, a Hindu and a Sikh officer in the dock together, and the Congress set up a defence committee including Bhulabhai Desai and Jawaharlal Nehru. Mohan Singh had founded the first INA in 1942.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India
questions.h: One of each faith: Shah Nawaz (Muslim), Sahgal (Hindu), Dhillon (Sikh).

questions.q: The Royal Indian Navy strike of February 1946 began on
questions.e: The ratings at Bombay struck on 18 February 1946 over racial discrimination and poor food and hoisted the flags of Congress, League and the Communists together. Patel and Jinnah persuaded them to surrender.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Cabinet Mission, 1946:
1. It rejected the demand for a separate sovereign Pakistan.
2. It proposed a Union with control over foreign affairs, defence and communications.
3. It proposed that the Constituent Assembly be elected by the provincial legislatures.
4. It said paramountcy over the princely states would be transferred to the Union government.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Cabinet Mission plan of 16 May 1946 favoured a loose Union, grouping of provinces and an indirectly elected Constituent Assembly. Paramountcy was to lapse rather than pass to the Union, leaving states free to negotiate their relationship.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Direct Action Day of the Muslim League
2. Formation of the Interim Government headed by Nehru
3. First meeting of the Constituent Assembly
4. Cabinet Mission announces its plan
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The plan was announced on 16 May 1946, Direct Action Day (16 August) followed, Nehru's Interim Government took office on 2 September, and the Constituent Assembly met on 9 December 1946.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q: In the Interim Government of 1946, the Finance portfolio was held by
questions.e: The League joined in October 1946 and took Finance; Liaquat's 1947-48 budget was dubbed the 'poor man's budget' for taxing business and industry. This irritated Congress members and strained the coalition.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q:
Consider the statements about Prime Minister Attlee's announcement of 20 February 1947:
1. It declared that Britain would transfer power by June 1948.
2. It announced that Lord Mountbatten would replace Wavell as Viceroy.
3. It was made in the House of Commons.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Attlee fixed a deadline of June 1948 and named Mountbatten as the new Viceroy; Mountbatten later advanced the transfer to August 1947 when violence mounted.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Mountbatten Plan of 3 June 1947:
1. A referendum was to be held in the North-West Frontier Province and in the Sylhet district of Assam.
2. The Punjab and Bengal legislatures were to meet in two parts to decide on partition.
3. A plebiscite was to be held in every princely state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The plan used referenda for the NWFP and Sylhet and split votes in Bengal and Punjab. The states were told to accede to either dominion, not to hold plebiscites; Radcliffe's boundary commissions drew the lines.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Independence Act, 1947:
1. It ended the suzerainty of the British Crown over the princely states.
2. It created two independent dominions, India and Pakistan.
3. It made the Government of India Act, 1935 inapplicable to both dominions from 15 August 1947.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act lapsed paramountcy and created two dominions. The 1935 Act, adapted, continued as the interim constitution until each Constituent Assembly framed its own, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 1

questions.q: Who succeeded Lord Mountbatten as Governor-General of independent India in June 1948?
questions.e: Mountbatten was the last Viceroy and the first Governor-General of India. Rajagopalachari was the only Indian to hold the office, until the Republic began on 26 January 1950.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 1

questions.q: Under the Instrument of Accession signed by princely states in 1947, the rulers surrendered which of the following subjects to the Government of India?
questions.e: The standard instrument transferred only three subjects to the Dominion. The states retained internal autonomy until they were merged or integrated later by V.P. Menon and Patel.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q: On 15 August 1947, when the country became independent, where was Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.e: Gandhi was in Calcutta, fasting and working to stop riots, after having spent months in Noakhali in late 1946. He did not take part in the Delhi celebrations.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q:
Arrange the following events of the Second World War period in chronological order:
1. Quit India Movement
2. Cripps Mission
3. August Offer
4. Individual Satyagraha
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: August Offer (August 1940), Individual Satyagraha (October 1940), Cripps Mission (March 1942), Quit India (August 1942). Each failed British offer led to the next phase of struggle.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Indian National Army (INA):
1. The first INA was formed in 1942 by Captain Mohan Singh.
2. Rash Behari Bose handed over its leadership to Subhas Chandra Bose in 1943.
3. The Provisional Government of Free India was proclaimed at Singapore in October 1943.
4. Subhas Bose formed the INA while still President of the Congress.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The first INA of Mohan Singh was dissolved in December 1942, and Subhas Bose took over the revived force in 1943 and proclaimed the Azad Hind government. Bose had resigned as Congress President in 1939, so statement 4 is wrong.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q: The Rani of Jhansi Regiment of the INA was commanded by
questions.e: Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan, later Lakshmi Sahgal, led this women's regiment. Aruna Asaf Ali and Usha Mehta are tied to Quit India.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the Constituent Assembly's first session on 9 December 1946 is correct?
o: The Muslim League attended and demanded a separate assembly for Pakistan on that day
Rajendra Prasad presided on the first day as permanent President
Nehru was elected permanent chairman at the first session
Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary chairman and the League boycotted it
questions.e: As the oldest member, Sachchidananda Sinha took the chair; Rajendra Prasad was elected President on 11 December 1946. The League stayed away, demanding Pakistan.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 1

questions.q: The Boundary Commissions for the partition of Punjab and Bengal in 1947 were chaired by
questions.e: Radcliffe, a British lawyer, drew the boundaries in about five weeks; the award was published on 17 August 1947, after independence, adding to confusion and violence.
questions.s: Spectrum, A Brief History of Modern India
